The question of this article is What do you need to know about a system to compute its output for any input signal? For the large class of linear, time invariant systems LTI systems , the answer is surprisingly short the response to a single, infinitely short impulse. The tool that turns this one response into every other one is convolution. Every signal is a superposition of infinitely many short impulses at each instant , one impulse with the weight . An LTI system responds to a shifted impulse with the shifted impulse response time invariance , and to a sum of impulses with the sum of the responses linearity . Therefore the output is the convolution , and describes the system completely. One principle behind all the results.
